questions.question: How does native CSS nesting differ from Sass nesting?
questions.answer: Native nesting runs in the browser with the same cascade and specificity rules, using & for the parent. Sass compiles nesting away at build time and adds extra features. Native nesting still increases specificity like descendant selectors.

questions.question: What problem does :has() solve?
questions.answer: It selects an element based on its descendants or siblings — a parent selector. Examples: styling a card with an image, a field with invalid input, or locking scroll when a dialog is open.

questions.question: What is the difference between @layer and @container?
questions.answer: @layer controls cascade precedence across groups of rules, replacing specificity wars. @container makes styles respond to a container's size, enabling reusable responsive components. They solve different problems.

questions.question: Why are logical properties important?
questions.answer: They express margins/padding/borders/insets in inline/block terms that follow writing direction, so RTL and vertical writing modes work without separate rules. They avoid physical left/right assumptions.

questions.question: What do dvh/svh solve and what is subgrid for?
questions.answer: dvh/svh account for mobile browser chrome when sizing to the viewport, avoiding 100vh overflow. Subgrid lets a nested grid inherit the parent's rows/columns so items align across components.

questions.question: Use :has() to remove top padding from cards that contain an image.
Why can :has() hurt performance?
questions.answer: The browser must re-evaluate descendant/sibling conditions when the DOM changes. Broad :has() selectors on large or frequently changing trees can be expensive; keep them specific and avoid animating related state.

questions.question: Why can mixing logical and physical properties cause bugs?
questions.answer: They target overlapping sides with different resolution rules, so margin-left and margin-inline-start can conflict or double-apply in RTL. Choose one system per codebase and migrate deliberately.
